questions.question: Users search a policy index for exact control codes such as PCI-07 and also ask questions in plain language. Which retrieval approach should you use?

options.text: Hybrid search with the semantic ranker
options.why: Correct. Hybrid combines keyword matching for exact codes with vector matching for meaning.

options.text: Vector search only
options.why: Vector search can miss exact strings such as codes.

options.text: Keyword search only
options.why: Keyword search fails when users word questions differently from the documents.

options.text: File search only
options.why: File search is for files in a conversation, not a company-wide index.

questions.explanation: Hybrid search covers both exact terms and semantic matches.

questions.scenario: A customer uploads their own contract to a chat and asks the agent questions about clause 7. The contract must not become part of the shared knowledge.
questions.question: Which capability should the agent use?

options.text: File search over the uploaded file
options.why: Correct. File search reads files attached to the conversation without adding them to company knowledge.

options.text: Azure AI Search
options.why: A shared index would expose the document beyond this conversation.

options.text: User profile memory
options.why: Memory stores facts about the user, not document content.

options.text: Web search grounding
options.why: Web search retrieves public pages, not the uploaded contract.

questions.explanation: File search suits content that belongs to one conversation.

questions.question: An agent should remember that a signed-in customer is vegetarian in later sessions. What should you configure?

options.text: Increase the model temperature
options.why: Temperature affects randomness, not persistence.

options.text: User profile memory scoped to the user
options.why: Correct. Memory scoped to the user stores preferences across sessions.

options.text: Add the preference to the shared knowledge base
options.why: That shares one customer’s data with all users and mixes memory with knowledge.

options.text: A larger context window
options.why: The context window ends with the session and does not persist.

questions.explanation: Memory holds what is learned about a person. Knowledge holds shared content.

questions.question: An Azure AI Search index feeds an agent from a Blob Storage container that receives new files daily. Retired files must disappear from answers. Which approach should you plan?

options.text: Copy the files into the prompt
options.why: This does not scale and cannot filter retired content.

options.text: Use file search for all documents
options.why: File search is per conversation and not suited to a shared library.

options.text: A scheduled indexer with deletion detection and a metadata field for effective date
options.why: Correct. The indexer keeps the index current, and metadata lets retrieval filter retired content.

options.text: Push documents once and never update
options.why: The index becomes stale and retired files remain.

questions.explanation: Plan ingestion refresh and deletions, not only the initial load.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of chunking documents before indexing them for retrieval?

options.text: To split content into pieces small enough to retrieve and fit in the model context
options.why: Correct. Smaller passages can be matched precisely and fit the prompt.

options.text: To encrypt the documents
options.why: Chunking does not encrypt anything.

options.text: To replace the need for embeddings
options.why: Chunks are usually still embedded for vector search.

options.text: To lower the quota on a deployment
options.why: Chunking has no effect on quota.

questions.explanation: Chunking prepares content for precise retrieval.
